Day 02
The Forbidden City & Jingshan Park & Bell and Drum Towers
▾
🗺Hotel breakfast → Forbidden City with a classic route → Visit the Treasure Gallery and Clock Museum → Jingshan Park → Evening tour of Bell and Drum Towers → Hotel.
✈ TransportPrivate car
🏨 HotelLocal 4-star Level hotel
🍽 MealsBreakfast
Forbidden City In-Depth Tour (3 hours) — Imperial palace of Ming and Qing dynasties, the world’s largest surviving ancient palace complex with profound historical heritage.
Treasure Gallery (45 mins) — Houses numerous royal gold, jade and precious artifacts showcasing exquisite imperial craftsmanship.
Clock Museum (45 mins) — Displays delicate ancient Chinese and foreign timepieces with unique artistic value.
Jingshan Park — Located north of the Forbidden City on Beijing's Central Axis, Jingshan Park was an imperial garden of the Yuan, Ming and Qing dynasties. Boasting five hills and ancient pavilions, it offers a stunning panoramic view of the Forbidden City from its peak. It is also famous for beautiful peonies in spring.
Bell and Drum Towers — Evening Visit—The iconic twin landmarks on Beijing’s Central Axis, beautifully illuminated at night with traditional eaves and red walls glowing against the dark sky. A perfect spot to experience old Beijing’s charm after dark.
Day 03
Free time at leisure
▾
🗺Hotel breakfast → Free time at leisure → Hotel
✈ TransportPrivate car
🏨 HotelLocal 4-star Level hotel
🍽 MealsBreakfast/Lunch/Dinner
No fixed itinerary. Private car and guide takes you anywhere you want.(8 hours service duration)
Recommended Local cultural streets：
Qianmen Street — Wander along the antique-style commercial street on Beijing's central axis. Admire traditional buildings and red lanterns, ride the vintage tram, visit famous old brands like Quanjude, buy souvenirs and taste local snacks.
Dashilar — This century-old lane next to Qianmen Street gathers intangible cultural heritage shops such as Tongrentang (traditional Chinese medicine), Ruifuxiang (silk) and Neiliansheng (cloth shoes). Wander through old hutongs, enjoy authentic snacks and experience the business vibe of the Ming and Qing dynasties.
Wangfujing Street — Famously known as Beijing’s "Golden Street", it is a time-honored commercial pedestrian street. Here you can shop for international brands, visit traditional old stores and taste various local snacks. It is a must-visit place to experience the city’s prosperity and culture.
Nanluoguxiang (South Luogu Lane) — A well-preserved ancient hutong with a history of over 700 years. It mixes traditional Beijing courtyard houses, local snacks, creative shops and trendy cafes.
Yandai Xiejie (Pipe Lane) — a historic hutong with flagstone streets and traditional courtyard homes—to soak in authentic old Beijing charm. Along the way, try local snacks: sugar-coated hawthorns, hutong yogurt, crispy tripe, and stewed pork with offal.
Shichahai / Houhai — watch the sunset at Yinding Bridge with distant views of the Western Hills; take a wooden rowboat on the lake as the water glows golden at dusk; relax at a lakeside bar with folk music and night views, immersing yourself in old Beijing’s evening vibe.
Recommended Parks：
Temple of Heaven — An imperial complex where Ming and Qing emperors worshipped heaven and prayed for good harvests. It is the largest and best-preserved ancient heaven-worshipping complex in the world and a UNESCO World Heritage Site
Beihai Park — An ancient imperial garden with the White Pagoda and a large lake. Visitors can boat and enjoy classical Chinese architecture close to the city center.
Yuyuantan Park — A large urban park with a beautiful lake, famous for cherry blossoms in spring. Ideal for a relaxing walk near the city center.
Day 04
Summer Palace & Exterior Views of the Bird's Nest & Water Cube & Mutianyu Great Wall
▾
🗺Hotel breakfast → Summer Palace → Sightseeing: Exterior Views of the Bird's Nest & Water Cube → Lunch → Mutianyu Great Wall → Hotel.
✈ TransportPrivate car
🏨 HotelLocal 4-star Level hotel
🍽 MealsBreakfast/Lunch/Dinner
Summer Palace Main Area Exploration (2 hours) — A UNESCO World Heritage Site and the largest imperial garden in China, located in northwest Beijing. Built in 1750 during the Qing Dynasty, it served as a summer retreat for emperors and empresses. The 3.09 km² complex features Longevity Hill, Kunming Lake, and traditional Chinese architecture, blending natural landscapes with imperial grandeur.
Mutianyu Great Wall — A UNESCO World Heritage Site and the best-preserved section of the Ming Great Wall, located in Huairou District, Beijing. Constructed in 1368 by General Xu Da, it stretches 5.4 km with 22 original watchtowers. Famous for its stunning mountain scenery, fewer crowds, and visitor-friendly facilities like cable cars and toboggan rides.
Mutianyu Great Wall Cable Car Up & Walk to Watchtower 14 (1.5 hours) — Cable Car Up: A smooth 5-minute ride to the wall’s upper section, offering panoramic views of the forested mountains and Great Wall snaking through ridges.
Mutianyu Great Wall Toboggan Ride Down (20 mins) — Toboggan Ride Down: A thrilling 20-minute alpine coaster journey down the mountain, with a safe, fast track through pine forests—perfect for adventure seekers.
The Bird's Nest (National Stadium) — Boasting a grand and powerful look, it resembles a huge steel nest. Shaped like an elliptical saddle, its interlaced steel frames look like woven branches. Silvery grey in daylight, it glows with warm golden lights at night. Inspired by traditional Chinese culture, it stands for vitality and inclusiveness.
The Water Cube (National Aquatics Centre) — It features a neat cubic shape, presenting an elegant and dreamy style. The exterior is covered with countless ETFE air cushions that look like floating bubbles. The building appears light blue under the sun, and shines with colourful lights after dark.

Day 06
Old Town & Modern Skyline Tour
▾
🗺Yu Garden → City God Temple → Lujiazui Skyscraper Cluster → Binjiang Avenue
✈ TransportPrivate car
🏨 HotelLocal 4-star level hotel
🍽 MealsBreakfast
Yu Garden — A classical Jiangnan garden built in the Ming Dynasty, featuring exquisite pavilions, terraces, rockeries and ponds.
City God Temple — The heart of old Shanghai’s folk culture. It is always bustling with worshippers and lined with local snacks such as Nanxiang steamed buns.
Lujiazui Skyscraper Cluster — Here stand the Shanghai Tower, Shanghai World Financial Center and Jin Mao Tower. The upward views are absolutely spectacular.
Binjiang Avenue — A free riverside promenade with fantastic views across the river towards the Bund.
Day 07
Stroll Around Shanghai & Enjoy Night Scenery
▾
🗺Wukang Road → Tianzifang → Nanjing Road Pedestrian Street → The Bund → Huangpu River Cruise
✈ TransportPrivate car
🏨 HotelLocal 4-star level hotel
🍽 MealsBreakfast
Take a long rest in the morning.
Wukang Road — A charming art street lined with phoenix trees and historic villas. The Wukang Building is a famous internet-famous landmark.
Tianzifang — A cultural alley packed with handicraft shops and cafés, blending local lifestyle and artistic vibes.
Nanjing Road Pedestrian Street — Known as China's top commercial street. It boasts century-old prosperity, where neon lights and time-honored stores come together.
The Bund — A gallery of international-style architectures. Across the river stands Lujiazui, featuring stunning night views.
Huangpu River Cruise — Sail along the river to admire the dazzling lights on both banks, with panoramic views of the Bund and Lujiazui.
